title: Cap. III Rat. 12: efficacious election from mere good pleasure destroys free choice
pass_a_gloss: Reason 12. If we posit that God efficaciously elects certain ones to glory from the mere good pleasure of his will, and not from foresight of merits, free choice will plainly be taken away. For since no one can resist the efficacious will of God, it will not remain in their free power to lose glory, who in this manner are predestined to glory. Such an antecedent will of God concerning the salvation of Peter and Paul having therefore been posited, either there will be in them an absolute necessity of doing those things which are necessary to salvation, for example of believing, of living piously, of persevering in faith and piety, and so of arriving at salvation itself, or the efficacious decree of God can be made void. Both absurd and impossible. Therefore we ought not to posit an efficacious election of some to glory, except from foresight of merits which will arise from free choice prevented by the grace of God.
pass_b_english: Rat. 12. If God efficaciously elects some to glory from mere good pleasure of his will, not from foresight of merits, free choice is plainly destroyed. No one can resist God's efficacious will — so those so predestined to glory will not keep free power to lose it. Posit that antecedent will for the salvation of Peter and Paul: either they are under absolute necessity to do what salvation requires (believe, live piously, persevere in faith and piety, and so arrive at salvation), or God's efficacious decree can be made void. Both absurd and impossible. Therefore we must not posit efficacious election of some to glory except from foresight of merits that will arise from free choice preceded by God's grace.
source_text: Rat. 12. Si ponamus Deum efficaciter eligere quosdam ad gloriam ex mero beneplacito voluntatis suae, et non ex praescientia meritorum, tolletur plane liberum arbitrium. Nam cum nemo potest resistere efficaci voluntati Dei, non manebit in eorum libera potestate gloriam amittere, qui hoc modo sunt ad gloriam praedestinati. Posita itaque tali antecedente voluntate Dei de salute Petri et Pauli, aut erit in illis absoluta necessitas operandi ea quae sunt necessaria ad salutem, puta credendi, pie vivendi, in fide et pietate perseverandi, atque adeo perveniendi ad ipsam salutem, aut Dei decretum efficax potest fieri irritum. Utrumque absurdum et impossibile. Ergo non debemus ponere electionem aliquorum efficacem ad gloriam, nisi ex praescientia meritorum quae orientur ex libero arbitrio per gratiam Dei praevento.
